tip: Two finished events, two past forms: έπεσα και χτύπησα (épesa ke khtípisa = I fell and hit).
Με τσίμπησε (me tsíbise) = it stung me – the stinger is the subject, you are με.
Η πίεση (i píesi) on its own normally means blood pressure: έχει πίεση (ékhi píesi) = he has blood pressure trouble.
Κόβω (kóvo) = cut, but also quit: κόψε το αλάτι (kópse to aláti = cut out the salt).
Greek 'closes' an appointment rather than booking it: να κλείσω ραντεβού (na klíso randevú = to book an appointment).
Παίρνω τηλέφωνο (pérno tiléfono) = I make a call: πάρε τηλέφωνο (páre tiléfono) = give them a call.
Σας usually pulls a second accent onto longer words: το τηλέφωνό σας (to tiléfonó sas = your phone number).
Greek has a verb for being late: άργησα (áryisa = I was late), and the amount just follows – άργησα δέκα λεπτά (déka leptá = ten minutes).
Μη (mi) plus the verb makes a negative command: μη φας (mi fas = don't eat) – no helper word needed, μη does the work.
After a command the 'it' follows the verb: κρατήστε την (kratíste tin = hold it).
Θα περάσει (tha perási = it will pass) means once and done – θα περνάει (tha pernái) would mean it keeps happening. Same verb, two futures.
Να (na) with the ongoing present = standing advice: να πίνετε (na pínete = keep drinking, these days).
Γράφω (ghráfo) here = prescribe: θα σας γράψω μια αλοιφή (tha sas ghrápso mia alifí = I'll prescribe you a cream).
Και after the verb usually means too/also: πάρτε και προβιοτικά (párte ke proviotiká = take probiotics too).
A written accent on μού (mu) marks 'to me': μού σύστησε (mu sístise = he recommended to me). Without it, μου means my: ο γιατρός μου (o yatrós mu = my doctor).
Περαστικά (perastiká) = get well soon – literally 'may it pass', said to anyone ill.
Εφημερεύει (efimerévi) = it's on duty tonight – pharmacies take turns, and the rota is usually posted on the door.
Κάθε οχτώ ώρες (káthe okhtó óres) = every eight hours – κάθε never changes form.
Με άδειο στομάχι (me ádhio stomákhi) = on an empty stomach – Greek says 'with' here.
Μήπως (mípos) softens a question: μήπως έχετε; (mípos ékhete = do you happen to have?).
Ορίστε (oríste) = here you are – say it as you hand something over.
Με πιάνει (me piáni) = literally 'it grabs me' – the medicine works on me.
Τα μεσάνυχτα (ta mesánikhta) = midnight – plural in Greek, like 'the midnights'.
Παλιά (paliá = back then) with the ongoing past form = used to: παλιά κάπνιζα (kápniza = I used to smoke).
Μικρός (mikrós) on its own can mean when I was little: μικρός αρρώσταινα (mikrós arróstena) = as a kid I'd get sick.
Old habits take a pair of ongoing past forms: κοιμόμουν και ξυπνούσα (kimómun ke ksipnúsa = I used to sleep and wake).
Κάνω το εμβόλιο (káno to emvólio) = get the vaccine – Greek 'does' vaccines.
Στην ώρα τους (stin óra tus) = on time – literally 'at their hour'.
Το δυάρι (to dhiári) = a two-room flat; τριάρι (triári) = three rooms – flats are counted by rooms, not bedrooms.
Τον μήνα (ton mína) = per month: εξακόσια ευρώ τον μήνα (eksakósia evró ton mína) – no extra word for 'per'.
